0.5 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard ( Part III ) specifies the requirements for medium flat rigid rectangular waveguides for use in electronic and telecommunication equipment.

INFORMATION

12.1 Ratio Between Inside Width and Height-The standard ratio of inside width to inside height is in principle 4 : 1. For some types of waveguides given in this standard the ratio has not been observed because a different value of ratio was already in extensive use.
12.2 Deviation on Inside Width and Height-Deviations for the inside width and heights are in principle + l/l 000 of the internal width. 12.3 Frequency Range-The frequency range indicated in Table 1 is from I.25 to I.9 fc (fc=cut off frequency of dominant mode ). For the working frequency range may be any particular type of application, smaller or greater than the frequency range given in the table. *Specification for hollow metallic waveguides: Part I General requirements and tests (f;r~?:ct rev&n ) .

5

W:.

4493. t Part III ) - 1982

12.4 Theoretical Power Rating - The values quoted are the theoretical breakdown values at a frequency 1.5 times the cut-off frequency ( assuming breakdown in air at normal temperature and pressure to occur at 30 000 V/cm ). The figures quoted include a power safety factor of two as well as allowance for a voltage standing wave ratio of 2.0. For other frequencies the values given should be multiplied by:

1.34 [ 1 - (&if)`]' 12.5 Attenuation - The maximum attenuation shall not exceed 1.3 times the values calculated from formula (1) in 5.1 of IS : 4493 ( Part I )-1979* at a frequency of 1.5 times the cut-off frequency. The values given in the table are for waveguides made of copper with standard resistivity pO= l-724 1.10-8 ohm.metre.

(5) The waveguides shall be visually examined and condition, design, workmanship, finish and markings shall be satisfactory. Both inner and outer surfaces shall have a clean bright appearance in accordance with current engineering practice and shall be free from oxidation The dimensions and tolerance thereon shall conform to values given in Table 1 read with Fig. 1. The waveguide tube shall be cut by means of a saw. The cutting process should be carefully controlled so as to avoid distortion arising from the cutting; and the use of a fine hrgh-speed saw is recommended

The waveguides shall be visually examined and condition, design, workmanship, finish and markings shall be satisfactory. There shall be no burrs, cracks, pits or other irregularities of the surface. NOTE 1 - For waveguides used in aviation, the climatic category with dry heat temperature as + 100�C; cold temperature as -65% and rapid change of temperature from -65�C to + 100�C would be applicable. NOTE 2 - For waveguides used on ground equipment ( fixed or mobile ), the climatic category with dry heat temperature as + 100�C; cold temperature as -40�C and rapid change of temperature from -40�C to + 100�C would be applicable. NOTE 3 - For waveguides used for general purpose in laboratory, the climatic category with dry heat temperature as +85X!; cold temperature as - 10�C and rapid change of temperature from - 10�C to + 85�C would be applicable. *Specification for hollow metallic waveguides: Part I General requirements and tests (.first revision ).
